summary: A Request is one record of somebody needing something from somebody else, between members of one organization. It carries a per-organization number, a type (access|question), an addressee, an optional project and deadline, a five-state lifecycle in which only the requester writes `granted`, an append-only thread and an append-only audit trail. The existing manager-only vacation feed at /org/{orgId}/requests becomes everyone's inbox: the page and the sidebar row open to every role, the vacation section keeps `view-requests` and the All scope takes the new `view-all-requests`. Most of this is already on the branch (commits 481a165, 6f2dbb5, ffa814d) — three tables, one defaulted column, the service, the controller, both screens, and the full 6/22/13 unit/int/e2e suite. What is not done is four defects the previous run's review found and one bookkeeping item it already fixed: the decline branch writes a RequestMessage without its `message_posted` event; the web page reads capabilities from an un-normalized role, so a legacy `member` loses controls the server grants; and two E2E absence assertions fire before the response they depend on has arrived, so they cannot fail. T4, T5, T7 and T8 carry that work; the remaining tasks own the code that must keep holding while it is done.

The three capabilities are registered in BOTH unions: MemberCapability + CAPABILITY_MATRIX in packages/validation/src/index.ts, Capability + ROLE_CAPABILITIES in packages/validation/src/roles.ts, with `view-requests` grants untouched. Granting `view-own-requests` to all four roles makes ROLE_CAPABILITIES.user and .viewer non-empty for the first time, which falsifies the `capabilitiesFor(...) === []` assertions in packages/validation/src/roles.test.ts — those become 'an unknown role gets exactly what viewer gets' rather than being deleted.

tasks.title: Schema and the one additive migration

migration.note: Three new tables (Request, RequestMessage, RequestEvent) and one new column with a default (Organization.nextRequestNumber INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1). No rename, no drop, no new NOT NULL on an existing table, no backfill. Read from infra/deploy.sh, not restated from prose: the pipeline applies the migrate task definition, runs infra/migrate.sh (`prisma migrate deploy`) at infra/deploy.sh:184 as a one-off task on the NEW image, and only then `tf apply`s the services at infra/deploy.sh:188 — so this schema is live while the PREVIOUS image is still serving. Three tables that image never references and one defaulted column are invisible to it, which is what makes that window safe. One migration per run: 20260901140000_requests_01_requests is it, and no second directory may be added.

tasks.description: Request carries the columns the Data Model table names, with Cascade on organizationId and requesterMembershipId, SetNull on projectId, assigneeMembershipId and resolvedByAccountId (a request outlives a hard-deleted project and a removed member — member removal is a soft delete, so the cascade does not fire in practice). Indexes: @@unique([organizationId, number]) — the database-level backstop for concurrent number allocation — plus [organizationId,status], [organizationId,assigneeMembershipId,status], [organizationId,lastActivityAt]. RequestMessage and RequestEvent each take @@index([requestId, createdAt]), the shape TaskComment and TaskActivity already use. No hash chain on RequestEvent: this is an operational journal, not the evidence of an executed contract, and claiming tamper-evidence it does not have would be worse than not claiming it.

tasks.title: API: create, list and read — numbering, scoping, filters and the two counters

migration.note: consumes T2's schema; adds none of its own

tasks.description: SessionGuard -> OrgScopeGuard on the whole controller; every query scopes by session.organizationId and organizationId is a required positional argument with no default in every service method — the path orgId is checked by the guard and never used as a selector. Creation locks the Organization row with FOR UPDATE, reads nextRequestNumber, writes the Request and its `created` event in one transaction, exactly as apps/api/src/kanban/tasks.service.ts:158 allocates Project.nextTaskNumber. Nothing slow runs under that lock: no HTTP call, no mail, no PDF. A membership or project id outside the caller's organization answers 404 with no `fields` key, never 403 and never a validation error, so neither can be probed across organizations; an ARCHIVED project inside the caller's own organization is the 400 `projectUnavailable` case instead — the two differ because only the second tells the caller something they are entitled to know. `viewer` is refused create with 403 `createForbidden` from the service, not from CapabilityGuard, because the guard cannot produce the spec's message. The vacation aggregation moves UNCHANGED into VacationRequestFeedService and the controller composes two sources, so the pre-existing behaviour has one owner and the new code cannot regress it. Requirement 42's status mapping is applied when reading that feed (open->pending, granted->approved, declined->rejected, cancelled->cancelled, all->every row, answered->none) and no VacationRequest column changes and no row is rewritten. An unknown `status` or `type` is 400, including the retired spec-10 values pending/approved/rejected — a silent fallback turns a typo in a URL into a page that looks correct. `type=vacation` is a choice of SECTION, not a filter over one array: requests is [] and the vacation block is unchanged; a caller without `view-requests` sending it gets requests: [] and no `vacation` key, an empty page and not a 403. Both counters are computed BEFORE type/status/projectId/q: `waitingOnMe` is non-terminal requests where the caller is the addressee irrespective of scope, `total` is requests matching the active scope alone so the page can tell emptyMine from emptyFiltered, and vacation.pendingCount stays the unfiltered pending count because it feeds the badge.

tasks.description: STILL TO DO, verified against the current tree: requirement 19 says EVERY message writes a RequestEvent with action='message_posted' in the same transaction as the RequestMessage row. There are exactly two RequestMessage writers and only one obeys it. postMessage writes the message at apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts:438 and records the event at :455. The decline branch writes its reason message at apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts:522 and the only events.record in that block is the status_changed one at :548, so after a decline requestMessage.count is 1 and requestEvent.count for action='message_posted' is 0. Requirement 25 makes the decline reason a RequestMessage 'posted in the same transaction', so requirement 19 applies to it, and requirement 21 makes the omission observable: the History panel of a declined request shows the status change and never records that the reason message exists. Fix: after tx.requestMessage.create in the decline branch, call this.events.record(tx, { requestId, actorKind: 'member', actorMembershipId: caller.membershipId, action: 'message_posted', newLabel: caller.displayName }) — the identical call postMessage already makes — leaving the status_changed event untouched, because state-machine invariant 4 requires EXACTLY ONE status_changed per transition and this adds a second event of a different action, not a second status_changed. The rest of the task is the code that must keep holding: every transition, edit, message and reassignment re-reads the Request row with FOR UPDATE through the shared helper at apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts:783 and evaluates its guard against THAT read, so idempotence is by construction and two concurrent grants cannot both succeed; answeredAt is written once on first entry into `answered`, resolvedAt and resolvedByAccountId once on entry into a terminal status; lastActivityAt moves on any message, any status change, any edit and any reassignment; `granted` is written by the requester or an admin and by nobody else including the addressee and including a manager who is not the requester; a party the route forbids gets 403 with the message named for that route and a non-party gets 404, and no route answers both for the same caller. Requirement 47: this task makes no outbound call of any kind and MailService is not imported.

tasks.title: Web: the request detail screen, thread, history and the four action modals
tasks.description: The thread and the history are two views of one record and are rendered separately: the thread is what people said, the history is what happened, and a message appears in the history only as the fact that one was posted. Descriptions and messages are plain text on write and rendered as text — no author-controlled markup exists anywhere in this feature, so there is nothing to sanitize. In a terminal status the composer and every action control are NOT RENDERED rather than disabled: a control the caller cannot use is not drawn. Disabling is reserved for the in-flight guard, released on both success and failure; the submit control is never disabled for validation, and an invalid submission shows every error and focuses the first invalid field. The inactive-addressee banner sits above the actions and the Reassign control is offered to admin and manager only. Components come from @ds via apps/web/src/ds.ts, tokens only — no hardcoded colour, and the only raw pixel values permitted are the 1px hairline borders the tree already uses (apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/projects/page.tsx:326). The textarea gap is recorded in dsGaps, not improvised further.

tasks.title: E2E suite, with TC-01-E2E-08 and TC-01-E2E-11 anchored on the response
tasks.description: STILL TO DO — two absence assertions that nothing can break. (a) TC-01-E2E-11 (e2e/tests/requests.spec.ts, the final block) reloads the page and asserts sidebar-requests-badge toHaveCount(0). The shell remounts with badgeCount initialised to 0 (apps/web/src/layout/requests-badge-context.tsx:39 useState(0)) and apps/web/src/layout/Sidebar.tsx:88 renders the badge only when badgeCount is truthy, so the node is absent before the GET .../requests it depends on has resolved and the assertion passes on its first poll. The preceding anchor is sidebar-requests-link, which renders synchronously from the session and says nothing about the fetch — if the server returned waitingOnMe: 2 for two granted requests, this would still pass, and the spec calls this case the regression witness for requirement 44. Fix: await the list response (page.waitForResponse on the requests call), or assert a post-response node first, before the toHaveCount(0). apps/api/test/requests-page.spec.ts:182 badge check shows the genuine shape, where the badge is showing its value in the same DOM when the check begins. (b) TC-01-E2E-08's `user` half asserts requests-vacation-section toHaveCount(0) after openRequestsPage, which waits only for requests-page — the outer div rendered before any fetch. requests-vacation-section renders only from data.vacation, so it is absent at mount and the assertion holds even if the server wrongly returned a vacation block to a `user`, leaving the UI half of AC-2 and AC-3 unproven at the only level that can observe them. Fix: wait for something only the response can draw — requests-empty-state for that user, or a seeded row — then assert the absence. The scope-toggle assertion in the same block is sound and needs no change: canScopeAll is a synchronous render from the session. Also in scope: TC-10-E2E-01 in e2e/tests/requests-page.spec.ts must SELECT the `open` filter before approving, because its purpose is to prove an acted-on card stays in view after it stops matching the active filter and it relied on the default being pending-only; under an `all` default the approved card matches anyway and the case would keep passing while guarding nothing. That is an edit to keep an existing guard meaningful, not a retirement. An agent's e2e run holds its own ports: `E2E_WEB_PORT=3100 E2E_API_PORT=4100 CI=1 npx playwright test tests/requests.spec.ts tests/regressions.spec.ts` from e2e — never the whole suite, never a borrowed dev server, and a busy port is not a stopped run.

buildFromZero: The Request, RequestMessage and RequestEvent tables and Organization.nextRequestNumber — nothing in the tree models a request between two members today.
The five-state machine with its actor guards, and the rule that only the requester or an admin writes `granted` — no existing entity separates 'I responded' from 'it works'.
The per-organization request number allocated under a FOR UPDATE on the Organization row (the pattern exists on Project, the application to Organization does not).
The append-only RequestEvent trail and the four action kinds it records.
Derived overdue, computed per reading account's timezone and stored nowhere.
The default comparator: non-terminal before terminal as the FIRST key, then blocking, then overdue, then priority, then lastActivityAt.
Three capabilities in both unions, and the first non-empty ROLE_CAPABILITIES entries for `user` and `viewer`.
30 new REQUEST_MESSAGES keys and the validators behind them.
The unified status vocabulary over two sections, and the 400 that replaces parseRequestStatusFilter's silent fallback to `pending` on this endpoint.
The counts envelope — waitingOnMe and total computed before any filter — and the badge that reads it.
The request detail screen, the thread, the history panel and the four action modals.
The inbox list page as a general inbox rather than a vacation feed, and the sidebar row that is now unconditional.

doubleBehaviours.behaviour: MailService records every send and performs none, so TC-01-INT-21 can assert zero
doubleBehaviours.whyItMatters: requirement 47 and AC-13 are negative claims — that nothing was sent. A negative claim needs an observer that would have recorded a send, otherwise the case passes because nothing was watching. InMemoryMailService is that observer and already exists (apps/api/test/clients.spec.ts:136); no new double is written.

doubleBehaviours.behaviour: the E2E mail sink at GET /api/test/mail/latest?email= stays unused by this spec's cases
doubleBehaviours.whyItMatters: this spec sends no mail, so a case reading the sink would be asserting the absence of a message on a channel it never uses. Named so nobody adds one.

dsGaps.resolution: the DS barrel (apps/web/src/ds.ts) exports Input but no Textarea, so the description field, the message composer and the decline reason each style a raw <textarea> with a 1.5px border and 12px padding — the two hardcoded sizes in this feature. Four screens already shipped the same workaround (apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/documents/templates/[templateId]/page.tsx, apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/members/[memberId]/RejectRequestModal.tsx, apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/projects/[projectId]/kanban/CreateTaskModal.tsx, apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/projects/[projectId]/tasks/[taskId]/TaskDetailScreen.tsx), so the gap predates this spec and this spec must not widen it further. Add Textarea to the design system with its border and padding as tokens, and export it from the barrel; never improvise a sixth copy per screen.

dsGaps.missing: no DS-gaps table in the spec itself
dsGaps.resolution: the UI Description says anything missing 'goes into the design system and is recorded in a DS-gaps table', and the spec has none. Recorded here instead; raised to the human as note P2.

risks.risk: The plan's four live items are all in code that already looks finished, so a reader skimming the diff sees a complete feature and stops. T4's missing event, T5's un-normalized role and T8's two unfailable assertions are invisible to a green suite by construction — that is what each of them is.
risks.mitigation: each is pinned by a test change in the same task: T7 extends TC-01-INT-11 to assert the message_posted event, and T8 re-anchors both E2E assertions on the response so they can fail. T5's fix has no test today; add a `member`-role case or accept the gap knowingly — e2e/tests/helpers.ts:164 types setMembershipRole to the four target values only, so the legacy value is never exercised anywhere in the suite.

risks.risk: Fixing T5 by widening setMembershipRole's type to accept `member` would let any test set a role the specs have retired, and the four-value type is itself a guard.
risks.mitigation: prefer hasCapability(session.role, ...) on the page, which normalizes without needing a test that produces a legacy row; if a regression witness is wanted, write it as a unit case over can(normalizeRole('member'), 'create-request') rather than by loosening the e2e helper.

risks.risk: T4's fix adds a second RequestEvent inside the decline transaction. A careless implementation writes a second status_changed instead, which breaks state-machine invariant 4 and AC-6.
risks.mitigation: the new event's action is 'message_posted' and the existing status_changed call at apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts:548 is not touched. TC-01-INT-11 must assert both counts separately — one status_changed AND one message_posted — so a merged or duplicated event fails.

risks.risk: Requirement 43 orders by `overdue`, which requirement 33 derives per reading account's timezone. Ordering therefore cannot be pushed into SQL, and an implementer optimising the list query later would silently change the order for readers in some timezones.
risks.mitigation: the comparator lives in packages/validation (compareRequestRows) and is applied after serialization; TC-01-UNIT-04 loads the terminal row with blocking, urgent, overdue and the newest lastActivityAt so it fails if non-terminal-before-terminal stops being the first key.

risks.risk: The area README states that soft-deleted addressees' requests 'surface in the reassignment filter', which requirement 36 explicitly says does not exist. An implementer who reads the README as instructed could build a filter the spec forbids.
risks.mitigation: requirement 36 is the rule: no reassignment filter, requirement 42 enumerates the filters exhaustively. Raised to the human as note P1 so the README row is corrected rather than re-argued next release.

risks.risk: TC-10-E2E-01 in e2e/tests/requests-page.spec.ts keeps passing after the status default becomes `all` while guarding nothing, because the approved card matches the filter it was meant to fall out of.
risks.mitigation: T8 selects the `open` filter before approving. This is the one existing E2E the spec edits rather than retires, and the edit is what keeps the rule it protects observable.

risks.risk: This branch already carries the migration 20260901140000_requests_01_requests. Any further schema thought — a column for overdue, an index for the reassignment filter — would be a second migration in one run.
risks.mitigation: one migration per run: neither is needed. Overdue is derived by rule and there is no reassignment filter by rule.
